# Meeting Summary: AI-Driven Marine Animal Rescue System

## 1. Overall Summary

Team Straw Hats presented their project, "PSID: KR305," an AI-based system for detecting and rescuing injured or stranded marine animals.  The system utilizes drone, satellite, and CCTV footage, along with crowdsourced reports and environmental data, to identify distressed animals, alert authorities, and guide rescue efforts.  The system features a crowdsourced reporting app, guided citizen rescue support, marine species recognition, environmental context integration, heatmaps for rescue route planning, and a live public dashboard.  The implementation plan involves multimodal data acquisition, processing using various AI models (YOLOv9, TCN, Transformer), and a hybrid edge-cloud system.  The tech stack includes Node.js, FastAPI, ReactJS, and various cloud services.

## 2. Key Discussion Points

*   Problem Statement:  Delayed detection of injured or stranded marine animals leads to missed rescue opportunities and animal deaths due to a lack of real-time monitoring.
*   Proposed Solution: An AI-driven system analyzing drone, satellite, and CCTV footage to identify and locate distressed marine animals, instantly alerting relevant authorities.
*   Unique Features: Crowdsourced reporting app, guided citizen rescue support, marine species recognition and data logging, environmental context integration, heatmaps and rescue route planning, and a live public dashboard.
*   Technical Approach: Multimodal data acquisition (drone, satellite, CCTV, acoustic sensors), data preprocessing using OpenCV, AI model application (YOLOv9 for object detection, TCN for behavior analysis, Transformer for data fusion), and a hybrid edge-cloud system for rapid processing.
*   Implementation Plan:  Detailed steps for data acquisition, preprocessing, AI model application, and alert generation.
*   Technology Stack:  Node.js, FastAPI, ReactJS, PyTorch, YOLOv9, TCN, Transformer, various cloud services (AWS), and data acquisition tools (DJI SDK, Copernicus, RadarSat, OpenWeatherMap).
